misconceptions.description: Assuming that more clicks, drags, or animations mean more learning regardless of what cognitive work they require
misconceptions.trigger: learner adds hotspots, carousels, or flip cards without specifying the thinking each interaction provokes
misconceptions.feedback: Interaction is instructional only when it drives generative processing. For each pattern, name the thinking it requires, not the motion it produces.

misconceptions.description: Choosing an unusual interaction pattern for distinctiveness even when a familiar pattern would lower extraneous load
misconceptions.trigger: learner picks a custom gesture or bespoke widget where a standard accordion or tab would let learners reuse prior interface knowledge
misconceptions.feedback: A familiar interaction pattern lets learners spend attention on content, not on the interface. Reserve novel patterns for when the familiar one truly fails the task.

misconceptions.description: Designing an interaction that accepts learner input but never responds to it, so the loop never closes
misconceptions.trigger: learner builds a drag-and-drop or selection step that shows no result, hint, or change after the action
misconceptions.feedback: Every learning interaction needs a visible consequence. Specify what the learner sees or can do differently after acting, or the pattern is decorative.

misconceptions.description: Treating an interaction as universally usable when its physical cost (precise dragging, rotation, hover-only reveals) is trivial for some learners but a barrier for keyboard, screen-reader, or motor-impaired learners
misconceptions.trigger: learner adopts a drag-precise or pointer-only pattern with no equivalent keyboard or screen-reader path
misconceptions.feedback: Run the equity test: can a keyboard or screen-reader learner perform the same operation at comparable cost? UDL's multiple means of action and WCAG 2.2 expect an equivalent path (such as select-then-place) so the interaction's cost does not fall asymmetrically on some learners.
